title: Interoperability catalog + automated validation pipeline for Terraform provider/module upgrades
creator: Lena Howard
description: Problem: Private (VPC) customers run a variety of Terraform module versions and provider combinations. Upgrading providers or modules has caused subtle runtime breakages (provider schema changes, provider plugin ABI differences, inadvertent state schema drift) and manual compatibility checks are time-consuming and error-prone. Goal: produce a single-source interoperability catalog that maps supported module versions, provider versions, and runtime constraints; and build an automated validation pipeline that continuously verifies candidate upgrade combos with smoke plans, state migration checks, and optional canary applies in isolated environments.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable interoperability catalog (git-backed) that lists supported module<->provider combinations, expected terraform CLI version ranges, and known incompatible pairs.

A CI pipeline that runs for any proposed provider or module bump which executes: terraform init+plan (with lockfile reconciliation), plan-diff rules, and automated smoke apply against a sandbox cluster when flagged.
Automated generation of .terraform.lock.hcl validation and a suggested provider version constraint patch for module repos (via PR template) when safe.
A documented rollback/runbook for state migrations triggered by upgrades, including a 'canary' namespace workflow and observable gating metrics.
Operational dashboard that surfaces unsupported or stale combinations and scheduled compatibility scan history.
No changes to production private customer environments without a signed-off compatibility record and successful canary run (or documented exception).
tasks: Draft schema for interoperability catalog (YAML/JSON) and store under infra/compat/catalog/ in repo
Implement catalog loader in infra-ci that decorates PR checks for terraform-module repos
Create tf-compat-checker job that: runs terraform fmt/init/validate, runs terraform providers lockfile compare, runs terraform plan against canonical test inputs
Build optional sandbox apply orchestration (k8s namespaces + ephemeral cloud resources) for canary executes
Add plan-diff policy rules to fail upgrades that add provider schema deletions or state V2 migration markers without migration hook
Expose compat scan results to a small Console dashboard and produce weekly report email to infra-eng and PM owners
notes: Design decision: prefer conservative provider constraints (e.g., >= x.y.z, < x.(y+1).0) for management modules and allow looser constraints for customer-facing example modules.
We will rely on terraform's existing .terraform.lock.hcl for provider checks but add a reconciliation step that flags lockfile drifts vs registry metadata.
Plan-diff rules will be iterated in a separate RFC; initial rules focus on: provider resource schema removal, provider type renames, required_providers changes, and major-version bumps.
For on-prem customers with strict air-gaps, catalog entries will include a note describing how to source provider plugins and an advisory cadence for offline upgrades.
